Count-clock implication and its abstract boundary

These are statements about an injective integer sequence. The canonical game is an intended application only if the stated additional suppliers are proved. This supplement defines the actual counterexample and fills the compactness/counting steps missing from the short release summaries.

Explicit abstract counterexample to signed balance alone

For n≥1n\ge1n≥1, write its residue modulo 170 as (10k+j), 0≤k≤160\le k\le160≤k≤16, 0≤j≤90\le j\le90≤j≤9. Call it low if

  • j∈{0,2,3,5,7}j\in\{0,2,3,5,7\}j∈{0,2,3,5,7} for 0≤k≤110\le k\le110≤k≤11;
  • j∈{0,2,5,7}j\in\{0,2,5,7\}j∈{0,2,5,7} for 12≤k≤1612\le k\le1612≤k≤16.

There are 80 low and 90 high residues. Set d(0)=1d(0)=1d(0)=1, and

d(n)=2⌊4n/5⌋+2on low residues,d(n)=2⌊9n/10⌋+3on high residues. d(n)=2\lfloor4n/5\rfloor+2\quad\hbox{on low residues},\qquad d(n)=2\lfloor9n/10\rfloor+3\quad\hbox{on high residues}. d(n)=2⌊4n/5⌋+2on low residues,d(n)=2⌊9n/10⌋+3on high residues.

The two phase images have opposite parity. Equal adjacent values of lfloor4n/5⌋lfloor4n/5\rfloorlfloor4n/5⌋ can occur only at (5k,5k+1), and the rule never selects both for the low phase. Equal adjacent values of lfloor9n/10⌋lfloor9n/10\rfloorlfloor9n/10⌋ can occur only at (10k,10k+1), always split between phases. Thus the sequence is injective. The isolated initial output 1 is not repeated. Direct integer bounds give n<d(n)≤2n+1n<d(n)\le2n+1n<d(n)≤2n+1.

Each period translates the 80 low outputs by 272 and the 90 high outputs by 306, with no within-phase block overlap. Consequently

R(x)=10x/17+O(1),A(x)=7x/17+O(1). R(x)=10x/17+O(1),\quad A(x)=7x/17+O(1). R(x)=10x/17+O(1),A(x)=7x/17+O(1).
